threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check your watch for tube times instead of relying on the bus app. You'll learn soon enough, mate.
Caught a glimpse of a guy in a clown suit trying to barter bus fare with a bag of chips. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a street musician playing violin to a crowd of kids learning breakdance at Weserstraße. That energy felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can overhear debates about the best Döner right next to a gallery opening. Only in Berlin do culinary opinions mix with high art discussions.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local by how they navigate BART delays. If they casually mention rerouting via Muni like it’s no big deal, they’re a true SF native.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today just as a pigeon swooped in and landed on the driver’s shoulder. They both seemed equally surprised. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just pop into a bar for tapas anytime. Most locals know you don’t get the best bites until after 9 PM, and half the places are closed for a siesta.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell newcomers by their struggle to navigate the winding streets; they often double back, staring at their phones like it's a treasure map.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie when they still flinch at the sound of a busker outside the station, expecting a quiet commute.
Caught a night bus last week and a guy was handing out fruit. Turns out it was all from his mum’s garden. Brixton’s quirks never cease to amaze.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The first time I spotted a cat lounging on a balcony, sunbathing as if it owned the place, I thought, 'Yep, I'm home now.'

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a hidden café serving €1.50 coffee, nestled between two graffiti-covered walls, with a cat that rules the place.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their tiptoeing past the Mission’s cloudy afternoons. Outsiders just pull on a sweater—they don't know it’ll burn off by noon.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a suit hold the Muni doors open for an elderly woman while she balanced a massive bouquet. Just a moment, but it felt so San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just Gaudí and parks, but it’s the hidden taverna on Carrer de Perill where the real local vibe is.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at crossing the street during the 'green man' phase. It's like they're waiting for a signal from the universe.
